messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> PD:INC-9821 on service/gpu-runtime (us-east-1) :rotating_light:
pagerduty: Alert details: sustained CUDA alloc failures (CUBLAS/CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY) across pool gpu-pool-5. Rate: 18/min, failing host set: [gpu-03,gpu-07,gpu-08]
alex: acked the pager. I'm on it. forwarding to oncall @maria for visibility.
alex: quick status — any customer-facing errors showing up in the LB dashboards?
jon: seeing increased 500s from inference route /v1/generate in us-east-1, error spike started ~2m ago. Latency for healthy hosts also creeping up.
linh: kvcache evictions spiked prior to alloc fails. suspecting fragmentation + long-lived cache entries.
maria: thanks. @alex, can you check nvml + dmesg on gpu-03 and gpu-07? I'll start rerouting traffic off that pool.
alex: running ssh and grabbing nvml output now.
ops-bot: running command: kubectl get pods -l pool=gpu-pool-5 -o wide --namespace=prod
alex: nvml output (excerpt):
```
GPU 03: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY (alloc 3.2GB)
GPU 07: GPU page fault, kernel 0x1f at 0x7ff.. stack trace truncated
Mem usage: 95%/100% on several processes (model-worker: pids 4123, 4124)
```
linh: logs show repeated model-worker attempts holding KV cache growth and never releasing for long sequences.
alex: taking gpu-pool-5 out of routing. kubectl annotate node gpu-03 maintenance=true; mark pool drain in router.
pagerduty: Note: first ack by alex, escalation to SRE lead if unacked in 10m.
maria: reroute done. traffic shifted to gpu-pool-2 and gpu-pool-8. keep an eye on tail latency.
jon: customer-impact: acme-payments had 42 failed requests in last 5m (they're on us-east-1 primary). ramped fallback to other region for them.
linh: starting rolling restart of model-worker on affected nodes (graceful drain) to reclaim kvcache and free GPU memory.
alex: applying quick mitigation: set env MODEL_MAX_SEQ=1024 for affected deployment to reduce KV growth. patch applied to canary (1 pod) first.
maria: canary looks ok, memory stable on that pod. rolling to rest of drained nodes now.
ops-bot: action taken: nodes gpu-03/gpu-07 cordoned; pod restarts initiated.
jon: error rate is decreasing but still elevated on some routes. PG bump (scale up) requested to add 2 more instances in pool-2 for capacity buffer.
linh: filed short-term follow-up issue: kvcache retention not expiring for long sequences. assigning to eng-runtime. ticket: RT-6142.
alex: handing off primary until 1718510600 to @maria (next shift), current mitigations: routing change, rolling restarts, canary config, autoscale request. Please escalate if OOMs reappear.
maria: ack handoff. I'll monitor for another hour, coordinate with runtime team for RT-6142.
pagerduty: Incident status -> acknowledged, escalation suspended. If error rate drops below threshold and no new OOMs in 15m, we'll auto-resolve.
alex: summary for post-incident notes: cause (probable): sustained kvcache growth + fragmentation causing per-process alloc failures; mitigations: drain pool, restart workers, temp seq cap, autoscale; customer impact: transient 5xx spike, acme-payments partially affected with automatic region fallback; follow-ups: RT-6142 (kvcache TTL), add eviction heuristics, improve node-level OOM alerts to include kvcache metrics.
jon: adding logs + graphs to incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incident/INC-9821 (draft).
linh: reassigning to eng-runtime for root cause. ping @runtime-team.
maria: closing loop — if anyone sees fresh OOMs ping me directly. great work team :thumbsup:
